candidate_nodes.label: prop:mw_ii_3_1_small_rank_orbits
candidate_nodes.remark: The proposition statement is legible in the span, but the source's exact notation for the character-expansion orbit set should be checked against the PDF before canonical admission.
candidate_nodes.source_note: Proposition II.3.1 characterizes Howe small rank in terms of the ranks of nilpotent orbits appearing in the character-expansion set attached to the representation.
candidate_nodes.statement: Let (pi,W) be a smooth irreducible representation of Sp(2n,F). Then (pi,W) is of rank k, for an integer k < n, if and only if every nilpotent orbit in the source's character-expansion set attached to pi has endomorphism rank at most k, and at least one such orbit has rank exactly k.

candidate_nodes.source_note: Lemma II.3.3 produces a representative of a nilpotent orbit whose S^2(X^*) component realizes the maximal rank allowed by the orbit rank.
candidate_nodes.statement: Let O be a G-orbit in g, and let k be the common rank of its elements viewed as endomorphisms of X plus X^*. Then there exists Y in O whose S^2(X^*) component has rank min(k,n).

notation_contexts.label: ctx:mw_ii_3_small_rank_setup
notation_contexts.statement: In II.3, G = Sp(2n,F) is realized on X plus X^* with X of dimension n. The unipotent radical N(X) of the Siegel parabolic P(X) is abelian and identified with S^2(X), so its characters identify with S^2(X^*). Orbits in S^2(X^*) are classified by rank, and Howe's notion of rank k for a smooth irreducible representation is recalled through vanishing on lower-rank orbits.

notation_contexts.statement: In II.3.3, a G-orbit in g has a well-defined common endomorphism rank on X plus X^*, and the lemma compares that orbit rank with the rank of the S^2(X^*) component of a suitable representative.
